key_insight: A porous lower wall adds a permeability-driven destabilizing effect that can outweigh the usual stabilizing influence of particle loading in Couette-Poiseuille flow.
engineering_relevance: Designing flow systems with porous boundaries requires accounting for particle–porosity coupling, since permeability can lower the critical Reynolds number and change stability trends.
method: Three-dimensional linear stability analysis of Couette-Poiseuille flow
Two-domain model: dusty-gas suspension in the fluid layer and VANS in the porous substrate
No particle penetration into the porous medium; coupled eigenvalue analysis of disturbance modes
evidence_signal: The abstract reports parameter-sweep stability results showing that higher permeability can reduce the critical Reynolds number and that additional coupled disturbance branches appear near the porous interface.
watch_item: The added unstable mechanism depends strongly on permeability, so conclusions may not transfer directly without careful calibration of porous-wall properties.
paper_title: Linear stability analysis of particle-laden Couette-Poiseuille flows: effect of porous walls
